rule: Adding -ed to words ending in y
objective: To spell the past tense of verbs ending in y
defs: spent time in a game or fun activity
remained in a place rather than leaving
reproduced something to match an original
made an effort to do something
responded to a question or message
held and moved something from one place to another
put something off or made it happen later

sentences.played: The orchestra ____________________ the final movement so well that the audience rose to their feet.
sentences.enjoyed: The whole class ____________________ the museum visit far more than they had expected.
sentences.stayed: She ____________________ at her aunt's farmhouse for the entire half-term, feeding the chickens every morning.
sentences.copied: He ____________________ the diagram so carefully that his teacher could not tell it from the original.
sentences.studied: The scientist had ____________________ the same species of beetle for twenty years before making her discovery.
sentences.tried: He ____________________ every flavour of ice cream on the menu before settling on the plain vanilla.
sentences.replied: She ____________________ to every letter she received, even when it took her several weeks.
sentences.obeyed: The crew ____________________ every instruction without question as the storm grew closer.
sentences.carried: The removal men ____________________ the grand piano up four flights of stairs in under an hour.
sentences.delayed: The verdict was ____________________ when new evidence arrived at the courthouse that morning.

starter.question: Can you add -ed to these verbs? What do you notice?
starter.ruleBox: Adding -ed to verbs ending in y: vowel before y — just add -d (play→played, enjoy→enjoyed). Consonant before y — change y to i, then add -ed (copy→copied, carry→carried).

thisWeeksWordsQ: What do you notice about today's words?
thisWeeksWordsPrompt: Look at each base verb. Does the y follow a vowel or a consonant?
thisWeeksWordsExplanation: All today's words are past tenses of verbs ending in y. The rule splits in two. Vowel before y: just add -d (play→played, enjoy→enjoyed). Consonant before y: change y to i, then add -ed (copy→copied). This is the opposite of the -ing rule — with -ing, y never changes at all.

clicks.label: Original meaning
clicks.body: Originally meant a large supply of something, particularly of writing material.

clicks.label: Then
clicks.body: Latin copia came to mean a transcript or replica. By the 1300s, copy meant a written reproduction.

clicks.label: Now
clicks.body: We use copied to mean reproduced something to match an original.

clicks.label: In today's words
clicks.body: Copy ends in consonant + y, so y changes to i before -ed: copy → copied.

wordSortQ: Can you sort these words into two groups?

wordSort.box1sub: The y follows a vowel — no change needed
wordSort.box2label: Consonant + y: change y to i, add -ed
wordSort.box2sub: The y follows a consonant — y changes to i
wordSort.hint: Look at the letter before y in the base verb. Is it a vowel or a consonant?
wordSort.answerNote: Vowel + y: played, enjoyed, stayed, obeyed, delayed. Consonant + y: copied, studied, tried, replied, carried.
wordSort.exampleLine: play → played (vowel + y, just add -d) | copy → copied (consonant + y, y→i then +ed)

wordShed.def: transported something by holding it and moving it somewhere else

wordShed.morphology: carry (v) → carried (past) → carrying (pres part) → carrier (n) → miscarried (past) → carriage (n)
